# Feature Engineering

## Overview
Feature engineering is the craft of transforming raw data into inputs that help machine learning models learn better, and it's often what separates a mediocre model from a great one. A 'feature' is any measurable input variable. Models generally need numeric input, so categorical variables must be encoded: one-hot encoding creates a binary column per category (good for unordered categories), label/ordinal encoding maps categories to numbers (appropriate when there's a natural order). Numeric features often benefit from scaling (standardization to mean 0 and std 1, or min-max normalization to a 0-1 range) so that no single feature dominates just because of its units. You can also create new features that expose hidden signal: extracting the day-of-week or month from a date, computing ratios, binning continuous values into ranges, or building interaction terms that combine two variables. Thoughtful feature engineering uses domain knowledge to give the model the most informative view of the problem, and it frequently improves accuracy more than switching algorithms.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: What features are and why they matter; Encoding categoricals (one-hot, label, ordinal); Scaling and normalization; Creating features from dates and text; Binning and interaction features. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
Practical Task: Take a dataset with categorical, numeric, and date columns and engineer a richer feature set: one-hot encode categories, scale numeric columns, and extract at least three new features from dates or combinations.
Mini Project: Build a feature engineering pipeline for a dataset (e.g., a housing or e-commerce dataset) that produces a model-ready feature matrix, documenting the rationale for each transformation.
Assignment: Take one raw column and create at least four derived features from it, explaining what signal each new feature is meant to capture.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.
